## Two Pollutants, Two Tracks in the Acid Rain Program

Under Title IV, the Acid Rain Program addressed sulfur dioxide and nitrogen oxides from the power sector through different regulatory mechanisms. Its sulfur dioxide system used allowances: each covered allowance represented permission to emit one ton under an aggregate cap, with allowances traded among participants.

Sulfur dioxide coverage expanded in phases. Phase I began in 1995 with 263 initial units at 110 plants. With substitution or compensating units included, the Phase I total reached 445 units. Phase II began in 2000, and the final cap, set in 2010, was 8.95 million tons.

The nitrogen oxides component followed a separate track for certain coal-fired units. It began in 1996 and was rate-based, without a cap or allowance trading. The program therefore used distinct mechanisms and timelines for its two pollutants.
